card.title: Power
card.says: the **rate** at which work is done or energy is transferred. For a constant force $F$ along velocity $v$, instantaneous power is $P = F v$.
card.from: dividing work $W$ by the elapsed time $\Delta t$; substituting $W = F \Delta x$ gives $P = F \dfrac{\Delta x}{\Delta t} = F v$.
card.useWhen: the question asks how fast a motor, hoist, or person delivers energy, or gives power in watts (or horsepower) alongside time or speed.
card.example: A hoist lifts a $50\text{ kg}$ crate $h = 4\text{ m}$ at steady speed in $\Delta t = 10\text{ s}$ (with $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$): $W = 50 \times 9.8 \times 4 = 1960\text{ J}$ → $P = \dfrac{1960}{10} = 196\text{ W}$.
card.analogy: Walking and sprinting up the same staircase do the exact same work against gravity, but sprinting finishes in less time and therefore demands higher power.
